title: "Category 3  Machine learning for time-series data"
description: "Learning from sensor, health, energy and industrial signals"

<span id="top"></span>

A **time series** is an ordered sequence of measurements. A wearable device may record acceleration every fraction of a second, an ECG contains voltage measurements from several leads, and an industrial plant records pressure, flow, temperature and energy over time. Machine-learning models can use these signals for classification, forecasting, anomaly detection and condition monitoring.

Many projects in this category use **self-supervised learning (SSL)** because useful labels may require expert work and are often scarce. SSL creates a training task from the unlabelled recordings: a model might align two valid views of a signal, reconstruct a hidden segment or predict a future representation. Other projects train directly for forecasting and study how a model represents time, channels and relationships among variables.

Evaluation depends on the task. Representation-learning projects measure label efficiency and transfer to new people, machines or operating conditions. Forecasting projects use chronological splits and test future prediction, robustness and computational cost. In every case, the split must respect the independent physical unit and the direction of time.

::: {.category-callout}
**Three ideas to understand**

Contrastive learning aligns valid views of the same recording. Masked modelling reconstructs hidden samples or patches. State-space models such as Mamba process long sequences efficiently. In multivariate data, a separate channel-mixing mechanism may be used to represent relationships among signals before temporal modelling.
:::

## Learn first and find ideas

- Representation-learning methods with code: [TS-TCC](https://github.com/emadeldeen24/TS-TCC), [TS2Vec](https://github.com/zhihanyue/ts2vec), [TF-C](https://github.com/mims-harvard/TFC-pretraining) and [SimMTM](https://github.com/thuml/SimMTM).
- Forecasting and sequence models: [DLinear](https://github.com/cure-lab/LTSF-Linear), [Mamba](https://github.com/state-spaces/mamba), [MambaTS](https://github.com/XiudingCai/MambaTS-pytorch) and [S-Mamba](https://github.com/wzhwzhwzh0921/S-D-Mamba).
- Data sources: [UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/), [PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/), [UCR/UEA archive](https://www.timeseriesclassification.com/), [Monash forecasting archive](https://forecastingdata.org/) and [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/).
- Monitor embedding variance and covariance from the first epoch in latent-predictive work. A smooth pretraining loss does not establish that the representation is useful.

## 3.1  Contrastive learning for wearable activity recognition {#project-3-1}

::: {.project-meta}
<span class="meta-label">Task</span><span class="meta-value">Self-supervised time-series representation learning, then classification</span>
<span class="meta-label">Level</span><span class="meta-value">BSc only</span>
<span class="meta-label">Compute</span><span class="meta-value">Light; CPU or 4 GB GPU</span>
<span class="meta-label">Data</span><span class="meta-value">[UCI Human Activity Recognition](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/240/human+activity+recognition+using+smartphones) — 30 subjects, 6 activities, 10,299 windows, 50 Hz, CC BY 4.0</span>
<span class="meta-label">Starting paper</span><span class="meta-value">Eldele et al., [TS-TCC](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14112), IJCAI 2021</span>
:::

::: {.project-intro}
**What you will do.** A phone records acceleration and angular velocity while a person walks, sits or climbs stairs. Learn an encoder from the unlabelled sensor windows, freeze it, and measure how few labels a small classifier needs to recognise activities.
:::

**Data.** UCI HAR is a 58 MB public download under CC BY 4.0. It contains pre-windowed 2.56-second recordings with 50% overlap and a standard subject-independent split. Keep that split.

**Methods and code.** [TS-TCC](https://github.com/emadeldeen24/TS-TCC) or [TS2Vec](https://github.com/zhihanyue/ts2vec) — choose **one**. Use the same 1-D CNN or small Transformer encoder for the self-supervised and supervised comparisons.

**Baselines and evaluation.** Random frozen encoder, SSL frozen linear probe, SSL fine-tuning and a fully supervised model trained from scratch. Report accuracy and macro-F1 on the subject-independent split.

::: {.scope .scope-bsc}
**Bachelor research question.** **How much labelled activity data can self-supervised pretraining replace?**

*Core experiment.* Compare all four conditions at 1%, 5%, 10%, 25% and 100% label budgets. Resample the labelled windows within the training subjects and report confidence intervals. Optionally test robustness by jointly rotating the accelerometer and gyroscope axes.
:::

## 3.2  Lead-aware masked learning for 12-lead ECG {#project-3-2}

::: {.project-meta}
<span class="meta-label">Task</span><span class="meta-value">Self-supervised multivariate time-series learning, then multi-label classification</span>
<span class="meta-label">Level</span><span class="meta-value">MSc preferred; BSc with a supplied data pipeline</span>
<span class="meta-label">Compute</span><span class="meta-value">Moderate; 8 GB GPU recommended</span>
<span class="meta-label">Data</span><span class="meta-value">[PTB-XL](https://physionet.org/content/ptb-xl/1.0.3/) — 21,799 ECGs, 18,869 patients, 100/500 Hz, CC BY 4.0, no credentialing</span>
<span class="meta-label">Starting paper</span><span class="meta-value">Dong et al., [SimMTM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.00861), NeurIPS 2023</span>
:::

::: {.project-intro}
**What you will do.** A 12-lead ECG observes the same cardiac event from different electrical viewpoints. Instead of masking arbitrary time patches, the model hides complete leads or anatomical lead groups and predicts their latent representations from the visible leads.
:::

**Data.** PTB-XL at 100 Hz, using the official patient-aware folds: 1–8 for training, 9 for validation, 10 for testing. The dataset is fully labelled, so label budgets simulate scarcity rather than reflecting missing annotations.

**Methods and code.** Start with [SimMTM](https://github.com/thuml/SimMTM) or [TS2Vec](https://github.com/zhihanyue/ts2vec) and a 1-D ResNet or compact Transformer. The [PTB-XL benchmark code](https://github.com/helme/ecg_ptbxl_benchmarking) provides preprocessing and supervised references.

**Baselines and evaluation.** Random frozen encoder, frozen probe, fine-tuning and the same encoder fully supervised. Macro-AUROC on fold 10 across the five diagnostic superclasses is the primary endpoint; add macro-AUPRC for class imbalance. Report patient-level splits and several label budgets.

::: {.scope .scope-msc}
**Master research question.** **Does lead-aware masking improve low-label diagnosis over random temporal masking?** Develop complete-lead or anatomical-group masking, condition the predictor on lead identity, and monitor embedding variance for collapse. Ablate masking granularity and predictor depth.
:::

::: {.scope .scope-bsc}
**Bachelor question.** **How does diagnostic performance change when fewer ECG leads are available?** With the supplied pipeline and one encoder, compare 12, 6 and 3 leads and lead II alone under supervised training and one established SSL method.
:::

## 3.3  Self-supervised forecasting representations for energy series {#project-3-3}

::: {.project-meta}
<span class="meta-label">Task</span><span class="meta-value">Self-supervised time-series learning, then temporal regression</span>
<span class="meta-label">Level</span><span class="meta-value">BSc or MSc</span>
<span class="meta-label">Compute</span><span class="meta-value">Light to moderate; 4–8 GB GPU</span>
<span class="meta-label">Data</span><span class="meta-value">[ETT](https://github.com/zhouhaoyi/ETDataset) — electricity transformer temperature, hourly (ETTh1/ETTh2) and 15-minute (ETTm1/ETTm2) subsets</span>
<span class="meta-label">Starting paper</span><span class="meta-value">Woo et al., [CoST](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.01575), ICLR 2022</span>
:::

::: {.project-intro}
**What you will do.** Pretrain an encoder on one unlabelled energy series, freeze it, and fit a small forecasting head. Test whether the representation transfers to a different series better than training a supervised forecaster on that series.
:::

**Data.** Use ETT with chronological splits and training-only scaling. ETTh1 and ETTh2 come from different transformers. The public repository uses CC BY-ND 4.0; cite it and do not redistribute modified copies.

**Methods and code.** [CoST](https://github.com/salesforce/CoST), [TS2Vec](https://github.com/zhihanyue/ts2vec) or [SimMTM](https://github.com/thuml/SimMTM) for pretraining. [DLinear](https://github.com/cure-lab/LTSF-Linear) is the required supervised reference; [PatchTST](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.14730) is optional. A ridge or linear head on frozen representations is the key diagnostic.

**Baselines and evaluation.** Seasonal-naive, DLinear, frozen SSL representation with a ridge head, and SSL fine-tuning. Report MSE and MAE at agreed horizons with identical input lengths and chronological splits, plus three seeds.

::: {.scope .scope-bsc}
**Bachelor research question.** **Do self-supervised representations pretrained on one energy series transfer to a different one?**

*Core experiment.* Pretrain on ETTh1, then probe and fine-tune on ETTh2. Compare with direct ETTh2 pretraining and DLinear trained on ETTh2.

**Interpretation.** DLinear may outperform the SSL pipeline. Analyse whether the gap changes with forecast horizon and target-data volume.
:::

::: {.scope .scope-msc}
**Master research question.** **Do decomposition-aligned positive pairs improve transfer and low-data forecasting when seasonal phase drifts?** Use a stable seasonal decomposition to select positives, compare with random cropping and frequency-domain contrast, and analyse non-stationary intervals. Validate the period estimate on ETT before adding irregular data.
:::

## 3.4  Self-supervised learning on heat-pump smart-meter data {#project-3-4}

::: {.project-meta}
<span class="meta-label">Task</span><span class="meta-value">Time-series representation learning, then household-level classification</span>
<span class="meta-label">Level</span><span class="meta-value">MSc preferred; BSc metadata-label version</span>
<span class="meta-label">Compute</span><span class="meta-value">Light to moderate after preprocessing</span>
<span class="meta-label">Data</span><span class="meta-value">[HEAPO on Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/15056919) — 1,408 Swiss households, 15-minute and daily resolution, 2018–2024; dataset licence must be confirmed</span>
<span class="meta-label">Starting paper</span><span class="meta-value">Brudermueller et al., [HEAPO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.16993), 2025</span>
:::

::: {.project-intro}
**What you will do.** Pretrain on household electricity series, then test whether the representations improve prediction of a household attribute or an inspection-derived issue.
:::

**Data.** The 458 MB public download contains 1,408 households; 214 have both smart-meter data and inspection information. Use the [official MIT-licensed dataloader](https://github.com/tbrumue/heapo). The Zenodo Rights field does not state a dataset licence, so confirm reuse terms before allocation. Group all splits by household.

**Methods and code.** Use [TS2Vec](https://github.com/zhihanyue/ts2vec) or [SimMTM](https://github.com/thuml/SimMTM), with a 1-D CNN or InceptionTime supervised baseline. Use heat-pump type for the lower-risk task, or one inspection-derived issue only after counting usable positives among the 214 matched households.

**Baselines and evaluation.** Compare random-frozen, frozen SSL, fine-tuned SSL and supervised encoders on identical household splits. Include weather-only and metadata-only baselines. Report balanced accuracy, macro-F1 and confidence intervals using repeated grouped cross-validation.

::: {.scope .scope-msc}
**Master research question.** **Can unlabelled data from a large related household population improve prediction on a much smaller labelled population, and do weather- and cycle-aware views improve it further?** Compare pretraining sources — none, labelled households only, unlabelled control households, and all households — then add outdoor-temperature-matched positives or whole-cycle masking and ablate the weather conditioning.

**Feasibility condition.** An inspection-label study has only 214 matched households. Select one primary label and verify its prevalence before committing to it; otherwise use the better-covered heat-pump-type task.
:::

::: {.scope .scope-bsc}
**Bachelor version.** Use heat-pump type or another well-covered metadata label. Compare supervised training with one SSL encoder on household-grouped splits and report a label-efficiency curve.
:::

## 3.5  Graph self-supervised learning from vibration signals {#project-3-5}

::: {.project-meta}
<span class="meta-label">Task</span><span class="meta-value">Graph-level classification (one graph per signal window) with cross-operating-condition transfer</span>
<span class="meta-label">Level</span><span class="meta-value">MSc only</span>
<span class="meta-label">Compute</span><span class="meta-value">Moderate preprocessing; small models on a 4–8 GB GPU</span>
<span class="meta-label">Data</span><span class="meta-value">[Paderborn KAt](https://mb.uni-paderborn.de/en/kat/research/bearing-datacenter/data-sets-and-download) — ~5 GB, 32 bearings, four operating conditions, CC BY-NC 4.0</span>
<span class="meta-label">Starting paper</span><span class="meta-value">Hou et al., [GraphMAE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.10803), KDD 2022 — [official code](https://github.com/THUDM/GraphMAE)</span>
:::

::: {.project-intro}
**What you will do.** Convert each vibration window into a graph of fault-related frequency bands, pretrain a graph encoder without labels, and test transfer to a different load or speed condition.
:::

**Graph construction.** Resample each window into the shaft-order domain. Use fixed nodes for BPFO, BPFI, BSF and FTF bands and their harmonics. Node features can include band energy, envelope amplitude, spectral kurtosis and RMS; edges can represent envelope correlation or spectral coherence. Fit thresholds on training data only.

**Data.** Paderborn provides 64 kHz vibration, speed, torque and radial load for 32 physical bearings under four operating conditions. Download it from the [official archive](https://groups.uni-paderborn.de/kat/BearingDataCenter/). Split by bearing, not by window. CWRU may be used only to develop the preprocessing pipeline; its official site does not state a clear data licence.

**Methods and code.** Use a GIN encoder with [GraphMAE](https://github.com/THUDM/GraphMAE). Compare with supervised GIN and a 1-D CNN. Do not remove fault-frequency nodes as a generic graph augmentation.

**Baselines and evaluation.** Compare a 1-D CNN, envelope-spectrum features with gradient boosting, supervised GIN, random-frozen GIN, and GraphMAE with frozen and fine-tuned heads. Test physics-based, similarity, random and no-edge graphs. Report accuracy and macro-F1; cross-condition transfer is primary.

::: {.scope .scope-msc}
**Master research question.** **Does a speed-invariant graph built from bearing kinematics transfer across operating conditions better than a similarity graph, and does self-supervised pretraining add value once the graph is fixed?** The contribution is the graph construction and controlled ablation; GraphMAE is a baseline.
:::

**Practical notes.** The dataset has only 32 independent bearings. Use bearing-grouped splits, report confidence intervals and keep the graph, SSL method and transfer experiment fixed in advance. This project is not suitable for a short BSc project.

## 3.6  Time–frequency contrastive Mamba for cross-condition bearing diagnosis {#project-3-6}

::: {.project-meta}
<span class="meta-label">Task</span><span class="meta-value">Self-supervised time-series representation learning, then fault classification</span>
<span class="meta-label">Level</span><span class="meta-value">MSc preferred; BSc with the processed dataset and a fixed comparison</span>
<span class="meta-label">Compute</span><span class="meta-value">Light to moderate; 4–8 GB GPU</span>
<span class="meta-label">Data</span><span class="meta-value">[Paderborn KAt](https://mb.uni-paderborn.de/en/kat/research/bearing-datacenter/data-sets-and-download) — 32 bearings, four operating conditions, 64 kHz vibration, CC BY-NC 4.0</span>
<span class="meta-label">Starting paper</span><span class="meta-value">Zhang et al., [TF-C](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.08496), NeurIPS 2022 — [official code](https://github.com/mims-harvard/TFC-pretraining)</span>
:::

::: {.project-intro}
**What you will do.** Use Mamba as the temporal encoder in TF-C, which learns jointly from time- and frequency-domain views. Test whether the resulting representation transfers between bearing operating conditions when only a small labelled set is available.
:::

**Data.** The official Paderborn archive contains vibration, motor current, speed, torque and radial load for six healthy, twelve artificially damaged and fourteen naturally damaged bearings. Begin with the processed FD-A and FD-B subsets provided through the TF-C repository. For the final evaluation, group the split by physical bearing or recording so overlapping windows cannot occur in both training and test sets.

**Methods and code.** Start from the [TF-C implementation](https://github.com/mims-harvard/TFC-pretraining) and replace its time-domain CNN or Transformer with a compact [Mamba](https://github.com/state-spaces/mamba) encoder. Retain the time–frequency contrastive objective and use a linear or small multilayer classification head.

**Baselines and evaluation.** Compare the original TF-C encoder, supervised 1-D CNN, supervised Mamba, random-frozen Mamba, frozen TF-C–Mamba and fine-tuned TF-C–Mamba. Report macro-F1, balanced accuracy, per-class recall and at least three seeds. The primary test is transfer to a different operating condition; report several labelled-example budgets and separate results for previously observed and unseen bearings where the data permit.

::: {.scope .scope-bsc}
**Bachelor research question.** **Under the same TF-C objective, does a compact Mamba encoder improve cross-condition classification or computational efficiency over the existing encoder?** Use the processed FD-A and FD-B data, fixed augmentations and identical splits. Compare accuracy, macro-F1, training time and memory without proposing a new pretraining objective.
:::

::: {.scope .scope-msc}
**Master research question.** **Can bearing-specific time–frequency views improve the transfer of Mamba representations across operating conditions and unseen bearings?** Develop one process-informed view, such as an envelope-spectrum view centred on bearing fault frequencies, an order-normalised view or a positive pair drawn from the same bearing under different conditions. Compare it with the original TF-C augmentations and ablate the view construction.
:::

**Practical notes.** The public code and processed data provide a complete starting pipeline, but the older TF-C dependencies may need updating. Test the Mamba environment during the first project week. The raw data are several gigabytes and are needed only for the MSc signal-processing extensions.

## 3.7  Correlation-graph Mamba for order-robust multivariate forecasting {#project-3-7}

::: {.project-meta}
<span class="meta-label">Task</span><span class="meta-value">Multivariate time-series forecasting</span>
<span class="meta-label">Level</span><span class="meta-value">MSc preferred; BSc evaluation version</span>
<span class="meta-label">Compute</span><span class="meta-value">Light to moderate on Weather; moderate on Electricity</span>
<span class="meta-label">Data</span><span class="meta-value">[Weather and Electricity](https://github.com/thuml/Autoformer) — public forecasting benchmarks with 21 and 321 channels</span>
<span class="meta-label">Starting paper</span><span class="meta-value">Cai et al., [MambaTS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16440) — [MIT-licensed code](https://github.com/XiudingCai/MambaTS-pytorch)</span>
:::

::: {.project-intro}
**What you will do.** Represent each signal channel as a graph node, exchange information between correlated channels, and then use a shared Mamba encoder to model each node through time. Test whether explicit channel structure improves forecasting and reduces sensitivity to arbitrary channel order.
:::

**Data.** Develop the method on Weather, which has 21 meteorological variables and 52,696 ten-minute observations. Confirm the result on Electricity, which contains 321 hourly electricity-demand series and 26,304 observations. Use chronological splits and fit scaling, correlations and graph thresholds on the training period only. The datasets and scripts are available through [Autoformer](https://github.com/thuml/Autoformer); [OpenTS](https://decisionintelligence.github.io/OpenTS/OpenTS-Bench/datasets/) documents their dimensions and standard protocol.

**Methods and code.** Use [MambaTS](https://github.com/XiudingCai/MambaTS-pytorch) as the main code base and [S-Mamba](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.11144) and [C-Mamba](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.05316) as channel-modelling references. Build a sparse top-*k* correlation graph from the training data. At each time step or patch, apply a shared GCN, GraphSAGE or GAT layer across channels; then apply the same temporal Mamba encoder to every node and a shared forecasting head.

**Baselines and evaluation.** Compare seasonal naive, [DLinear](https://github.com/cure-lab/LTSF-Linear), channel-independent Mamba, MambaTS and one existing channel-aware Mamba model. Graph controls must include identity, random and shuffled-correlation adjacency. Report MSE and MAE at standard horizons, three seeds, parameter count, training time and memory. Consistently permute the input channels, graph and outputs to measure order sensitivity, and mask channels at test time to measure robustness.

::: {.scope .scope-bsc}
**Bachelor research question.** **How sensitive are existing Mamba forecasters to channel order, and do their channel-interaction mechanisms improve over channel-independent Mamba?** Reproduce MambaTS or S-Mamba on Weather and compare channel-independent and channel-aware variants under channel permutations and missing-channel tests. A new graph architecture is not required.
:::

::: {.scope .scope-msc}
**Master research question.** **Can a sparse correlation-graph channel mixer improve forecasting and reduce sensitivity to arbitrary variable ordering compared with existing Mamba channel-mixing methods?** Implement the graph module, match model capacity, and ablate graph type, sign handling, sparsity and message-passing depth on Weather and Electricity. A window-dependent graph is an optional extension after the fixed-graph study.
:::

**Practical notes.** Use Weather for development and a sparse graph for Electricity. Correlation describes statistical association rather than a physical or causal link. A consistent relabelling of nodes, adjacency and outputs should not materially change a correctly implemented shared graph–Mamba model.
